title: The full cohomological-dimension condition is a bound on the pro-étale cohomology of the base-changed source
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, let $\overline X,Y$ be finite-type $S$-schemes, let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism, and let $c\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Use the constant-ring module categories, the pullbacks, and $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension], on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with finite-level derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

An object $W$ of a site is weakly contractible if evaluation at $W$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Then $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ is equivalent to the following cohomology test: for every object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, every affine weakly contractible object $W\to V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A_{\overline X}$-modules on $\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and every integer $r>c$, one has
$$
 H^r\bigl((\overline X\times_Y W)_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_Y W}\bigr)=0.
$$
Here $\overline X_V=\overline X\times_YV$, $p_V:\overline X_V\to V$ is the projection, and $\mathcal F_V=\mathcal F|_{\overline X_V}$ is the module pullback. The restriction in the displayed formula is the successive restriction of $\mathcal F_V$ to $\overline X_V\times_VW=\overline X\times_YW$. For a scheme $T$ and a module sheaf $G$, $H^r(T_{\mathrm{proet}},G)$ means the $r$-th right derived functor of global sections in the category of $A_T$-module sheaves (equivalently, the cohomology of global sections of an injective resolution). There is no finite-type assumption on $V$ or $W$, and $\mathcal F$ is quantified on the original source, with no constructibility or etale-origin restriction. The cohomology test is on affine weakly contractible $W$, not on all base objects without this restriction.

proof.text: Fix $V\to Y$, $\mathcal F$, and $r>c$, and put $K_V=\iota\mathcal F_V$. On the chosen small skeleton of $(\overline X_V)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the coefficient sheaf $A_{\overline X_V}$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] its module category is Grothendieck abelian, so [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] gives enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to $K_V$, whose cohomology is concentrated in degree zero, obtaining a representing complex $I_V^\bullet$ of injective module sheaves with $I_V^i=0$ for $i<0$. That node also says this complex is K-injective. Thus the finite-level definition [def-weil-derived-direct-image] computes $R(p_V)_*K_V$ by the actual complex $(p_V)_*I_V^\bullet$. All these constructions use the same constant coefficient ring $A$; the category is not replaced by etale sheaves or by constructible sheaves.

Let $W\to V$ be affine and weakly contractible in $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and write $Z=\overline X_V\times_VW$. The projection $Z\to\overline X_V$ is weakly etale: $W\to V$ is weakly etale by the site definition, and weakly etale maps are stable under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] identifies $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the localized site and says that restriction is exact and preserves injectives. The restricted complex $I_V^\bullet|_Z$ is bounded below and termwise injective. Exactness of restriction gives $\mathcal H^0(I_V^\bullet|_Z)\cong\mathcal F|_Z$ and $\mathcal H^i(I_V^\bullet|_Z)=0$ for $i\ne0$, by applying restriction to the representative isomorphism from step 1. Thus it represents the degree-zero sheaf $\mathcal F|_Z$. Its global-section cohomology is $H^r(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F|_Z)$. By the sectionwise formula in [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], there is an equality of complexes $((p_V)_*I_V^\bullet)(W)=\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},I_V^\bullet|_Z)$; in degree $i$ both sides are $I_V^i(Z)$, and their differential is the same map $d^i_Z:I_V^i(Z)\to I_V^{i+1}(Z)$, because the definition specifies $((p_V)_*d^i)_W=d^i_Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact] on $V$, with coefficient sheaf $A_V$: its hypothesis is exactly the stipulated weak contractibility of $W$. Evaluation therefore commutes with the homology of $(p_V)_*I_V^\bullet$. With [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] this gives
$$
 \bigl(\mathcal H^r(R(p_V)_*\iota\mathcal F_V)\bigr)(W)
 \cong H^r\bigl(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F|_Z\bigr).
$$
The fibre-product identity $Z=\overline X\times_YW$ is its defining universal-property identification. Since $r>c\geq0$, only positive-degree cohomology is used. No collapse of Leray over an arbitrary $V$ is asserted.

proof.text: Use [cor-sf-fullcd-weakly-contractible-test] with precisely the coefficient $A$, the proper $S$-morphism $p$, and the nonnegative integer $c$ of the statement. If $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ holds, that node gives zero for every relative evaluation on the left of the comparison in step 2; its right side is therefore zero for all $V,W,\mathcal F,r$ in the cohomology test. Conversely, assume the cohomology test. Step 2 makes all the relative evaluations in the corollary zero. Take $V=Y$ with its identity map as well: $p_V=p$ and $\mathcal F_V=\mathcal F$ under the canonical identity fibre-product identifications, so the absolute evaluations in the corollary are also zero. These are every clause, with exactly the same quantifiers, of the corollary's evaluation test. Its converse gives $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$. In particular no sheaf on a base-changed source that is not a pullback of an original-source sheaf has been introduced into the quantifier.

Corrected the etale-only direct-image definition citation.
